findings.requirement: A merge is never green while an affected acceptance test lacks a passing run on the current identity
findings.what: Check 2 and bookkeeping: reversed or reworded confirmed examples are listed in examples_kept without a reason. SR-127/EX-3 (3 linked tests: the merge is NOT blocked by an unshown proof), SR-093/EX-2 (the owner is asked nothing about success) and SR-020/EX-1 (a regression and the owner is asked) are now inverted by the draft (merge refuses; owner decides the proof; owner is not asked), and SR-093/EX-1 (the intent card shows 'Done when:') lost its card (P12). P10 and P5 authorise the changes, so this is not a contradiction, but each should sit in examples_dropped (or a 'changed' list) with the reason, otherwise the old behaviour the code still has has no recorded replacement. The same applies to SR-031/EX-3 (owner runs plumb tests waive in a terminal; now a question-tool answer, exit 3 for the agent marker is not carried).

findings.requirement: A merge is never green while an affected acceptance test lacks a passing run on the current identity
findings.what: Check 4: the outcomes of 'full verification pending' are not distinguished. Example 9 (conftest.py breaks a helper) only holds and exits 5 with no run; example 11 (pyproject.toml) has the question tool ask run-or-waive; example 13 (uv.lock) runs the suite once with no question. The draft also merges the report-only form (SR-031/SR-047 validate --merge) with the running form (SR-048 merge-check) under 'the merge check', so a reader cannot tell when the suite runs, when the owner is asked and when it only holds. State the rule once (who runs it, when the owner is asked) and make the examples agree.

findings.requirement: Every requirement carries the proof the owner chose, and done and the merge refuse without its evidence
findings.what: Check 3: two behaviours in one. Examples 8 and 9 (a 'done when' item no example covers is named as a gap, then the gap goes) are the alignment check of SR-093, which the statement never mentions; and example 3 folds the 'done when' item into the proof ('its proof records ...') while examples 8 and 9 still treat 'done when' as a separate item. Either state the alignment gap in the statement and keep it as its own requirement, or say that done-when is the proof and drop the gap wording. SR-093's statement behaviour of telling the agent what a request leaves open (scope, non-goals, failure cases, not only success) is also not carried or listed as dropped (SR-093 has no linked tests, so low weight).

findings.requirement: Each turn's changes are verified by targeted covering tests, not the full suite
findings.what: Check 3 and statement mismatch: the requirement bundles selection from the map, exact-match evidence reuse (examples 6, 7), the stop hook delegating to the agent (examples 12, 13), the owner-set time budget (example 14) and the shared-infrastructure pending flag (example 9). The statement says nothing about the bounded sample, the pending flag, the timeout recording or the fresh-clone case that examples 9 to 12 assert. Evidence reuse and the hook's one ask are separate behaviours; at least say them in the statement, or split.

findings.requirement: Every requirement carries the proof the owner chose, and done and the merge refuse without its evidence

findings.requirement: A merge is never green while an affected acceptance test lacks a passing run on the current identity
findings.what: Wording: the statement says a failure 'stays until a run passes it', but confirmed SR-030/EX-5 (not superseded here) says a pass on a rewritten test body marks the regression hidden and only a pass on the original body resolves it. The examples do not collide with it, but the statement is too broad; say 'a run of the test that failed'. Also the regression rule drops 'or passed flaky' (SR-020, DEC-010), while DEC-010's retirement reason claims the examples state it.
